phase1_errors_found.issue: The #textinputext note says StartTextInput/StopTextInput 'have no visible effect' on desktop platforms. Text input is a mode: on Win32 the event mapper consumes every WM_CHAR without a TextInputEvent until the window's mode is enabled by StartTextInput, and the mapper's own comment says a game that never called it sees the same on every other backend.

The #mouse table describes MouseState X and Y as 'window pixels'. Mouse::GetState converts the window-client position to logical game coordinates through the window's renderer transform (letterboxing, virtual resolution); it equals window pixels only when no transform applies.

Accelerometer/Gyroscope support policy: Android, iOS or Desktop target, then ProbeIsSupported (acquire Sensor subsystem, IsAvailable, release); Compass needs rotation vector plus magnetic field, Motion needs an attitude source plus gravity, linear acceleration and gyroscope, both only on Android; MaxSensorCount is 10 per class.

Per-instance platform lease is acquired on first Start, kept across Stop and released only in Dispose; failed Start rolls back a lease acquired in the same call; Stop takes the shared session out only when the last started instance leaves, destroying it outside the mutex (platform contract: session destruction is a callback barrier).

Reading production: 9.80665 m/s2 to G conversion, wall-clock timestamps, software throttle (default 2 ms) compared in 100-ns ticks, Android landscape remap with opt-out, CurrentValueChanged before ReadingChanged from a pre-copied handler list; handler exceptions go to NativeDiagnosticSink (debug-build log line only).

Gyroscope.cpp and Accelerometer.cpp compared after stripping comments and normalising the class name: lifecycle code identical; differences are exception type, raw rotation rate instead of the gravity division, no ReadingChanged, and the rate remap. Compass.cpp and Motion.cpp likewise differ only in messages and getIsAttitudeNorthReferencedProperty.

Documentation drift: docs/devices-event-contract.md still says the Android bridge swallows handler exceptions with no logging, but AndroidSensorBridge::Run routes them through NativeDiagnosticSink at TARGET (DEVPERF-005); docs/devices-thread-safety.md attributes the instance counter to a static instanceCountMutex_, true for Compass/Motion but Accelerometer/Gyroscope count under the subsystem mutex.

Android backends: Compass uses rotation vector + magnetic field; Motion constructs six bridges, starts at most five, publishes only when four sources are within a 500 ms window (dropped frames counted), fused timestamp equals the attitude timestamp; bridge worker constants: 100 ms poll, 64 events per pass, 5 consecutive getEvents failures stop it, 5 s startup handshake and Stop bound, abandoned_ is permanent.
A start superseded by Stop tears down what it started but returns without throwing (only a failed start throws).

VibrateController: XNA API is Start(duration), Stop and getDefaultProperty; intensity, left/right, support and name are CNAEXT; duration validated 0-5 s and magnitudes clamped with NaN to zero before locking; PlatformVibrateBackend does not release a stale platform's lease when the platform changes.

DevicesShutdownCoordinator: no production caller of Shutdown() at TARGET (only tests and tools/devices/shutdown_ordering_harness.cpp); the harness returns 0 whenever main completes, so outside sanitizer builds the ordering tests show no crash or hang only.
Host tests cannot compile the Android bridge, backends or worker (all under __ANDROID__); only pure helpers and non-Android answers are reachable, plus fake backends for Compass and Motion.

contradictions.developer_claim: Matrix::CreateLookAt constructs camera axes from camera-to-target and up vectors, places them in M11..M33 and negative dot products in M41..M43.
contradictions.target_fact: The backward axis is normalize(cameraPosition - cameraTarget), i.e. target-to-camera, not camera-to-target; right = normalize(cross(up, backward)), up = cross(backward, right). The axes fill the first three columns (M11,M21,M31 right; M12,M22,M32 up; M13,M23,M33 backward) and M41..M43 hold the negated dot products with the position.

contradictions.developer_claim: Before a client handshake has assigned wire IDs, a public LocalNetworkGamer::SendData can reach ENetBackend::SendAppData.
contradictions.target_fact: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData never calls the backend: every overload only appends a PacketSend NetworkEvent to the session queue, and NetworkSession::Update drains it and calls SendAppData (SystemLink only). The pre-handshake queue is therefore reached when a queued send is drained before its ends are wired (ConnectToHost without waiting, Emscripten where EndJoin does not wait, or a gamer introduced later), not by a send after a native Join that already waited for the welcome.

phase1_errors_found.issue: States that Ctrl+C/Z/S 'are signals or flow control unless the terminal's keyboard protocol reports them'. While a TerminalSession is active (the whole run of a SOFTWARE game on a TTY), raw mode clears ISIG and IXON, so these arrive as control-chord key events, not signals or flow control.
Says 'the back buffer is columns x 8 by rows x 16 pixels'. The window keeps the game's requested size until the first SIGWINCH-driven resize; only then does it become columns*8 by rows*16.
Minor: 'one colour pair plus one glyph per cell' - the writer emits a foreground colour only (and no colour escape for Monochrome), no background.

contradictions.developer_claim: At startup the platform attaches EGL/Vulkan/presenter/dialog services where available.
contradictions.target_fact: EGL, Vulkan, dialogs and the idle inhibitor are created at startup; a wl_shm presenter is created per window on demand by CreateSurfacePresenter. Only the surfacePresentation flag is decided at startup, from wl_shm plus XRGB8888 seen during the second startup roundtrip.

contradictions.developer_claim: RecordSerial stores recent input serials; activation, cursor shape, drag/selection and window menu routes consult them.
contradictions.target_fact: RecordSerial keeps only the latest serial and its seat. It is consumed by xdg-activation, clipboard/primary-selection ownership, the window menu and the built-in frame's interactive move/resize. Cursor changes (wl_pointer.set_cursor, cursor-shape-v1) use each pointer's own enter serial.
contradictions.evidence: WaylandPlatform.cpp (RecordSerial, GetLatestInputSerial, RequestActivation); WaylandWindow.cpp (ShowWindowMenu, BeginMove, BeginResize); WaylandDataDevice.cpp (set_selection); WaylandMouse.cpp (enterSerial)

contradictions.developer_claim: If input vanishes after hide/show or a surface recreation, inspect surface-to-window mapping and seat attachment.
contradictions.target_fact: The wl_surface and its surface-to-window mapping live for the whole WaylandWindow; Hide/Show only destroys and recreates the xdg_surface/xdg_toplevel role. There is no surface recreation.
contradictions.evidence: WaylandWindow.hpp (class comment 'Lifetime of the objects'); WaylandWindow.cpp (constructor MapSurface, DestroyRole, ReleaseNativeObjects)
contradictions.resolution: corrected on the page (diagnosis now points at focus, seat attachment and configure path)

contradictions.developer_claim: EGL, Vulkan and wl_shm are three independent integration seams serving different renderer families.
contradictions.target_fact: EGL serves the EasyGL identities and OPENGL4 (needsGlContext) and Vulkan serves VULKAN (needsVulkanSurface), but no stock renderer reaches the wl_shm presenter inside a Game on Wayland: GraphicsDevice gives a CPU family a window and presenter only when surfacePresentation is true and nativeWindowHandle is false (the terminal). The presenter is exercised by tests, the validation harness presenter scenario and direct IPlatform::CreateSurfacePresenter callers.

contradictions.developer_claim: No signal handler, locale mutation, environment variable or alternate display server is installed by this backend.

Compose tables are looked up by LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG without setlocale.

contradictions.developer_claim: Vulkan and SDL_gpu have their own command/submission synchronization.
contradictions.target_fact: No CPU-side lock guards VulkanRenderer state (one static atomic for adapter sample counts); its synchronization is GPU-side fence-gated retirement of resource handles. SdlGpuModern.cpp states the SDL_gpu renderer is single-threaded and its registries take no lock; the only mutex there guards the optional shader-cross session count.
contradictions.resolution: corrected on the page: scoped to GPU-side retirement for Vulkan and the documented single-threaded contract for SDL_gpu.

contradictions.developer_claim: OnComponentRemoved nulls entries in the in-flight snapshot so a removed-and-freed component is not called later in the frame (stated without qualification about the calling thread).
contradictions.target_fact: The snapshot loops in Update/Draw iterate without the lock, and GameComponentCollection has no lock, so the nulling protects removal by code on the loop thread only; removal from another thread while the loop iterates is not synchronized.

contradictions.developer_claim: ALSA's worker is joined by Close before mixer state is freed; its own mix path uses a recursive mutex shared with setters.
contradictions.target_fact: The join is in AlsaAudioDevice::StopLocked (called by Close); the recursive mutex belongs to the CNA mixer engine that is paired with ALSA (MixerEngine.cpp in Backend/CnaMixer), shared with every facade call and with the device callback, not to the device.
contradictions.resolution: attribution corrected on the page (device barrier and mixer-engine lock described separately).

contradictions.developer_claim: Compass/Motion's Android route captures a shared control block ... (implies a general route).
contradictions.target_fact: Compass::getIsSupportedProperty returns false off Android and a backend is created only under __ANDROID__ (or installed by a test); the control block protocol is therefore Android-only in production.
contradictions.resolution: made explicit on the page; real-Android behaviour beyond the fake-backend seam recorded as unverified by CNA's own document.

new_pages.title: Maintainer Handbook
new_pages.purpose: Task-oriented recipes for changing CNA safely: fix a renderer bug, change public XNA behaviour, modify a platform backend, add a regression test, update the C API, make a release.

new_pages.title: I need to fix a renderer bug
new_pages.purpose: A recipe for fixing renderer defects: identify identity, family and host, separate shared neutral logic from one translation layer with a second backend, use the right harnesses and gates, and prove the fix.

new_pages.title: I need to change public XNA behavior
new_pages.purpose: A recipe for changing the XNA-shaped surface: where it lives, how to establish what real XNA does when references disagree, the CNAEXT marker, recording a deliberate difference, and the C ABI, content and test ripple.

new_pages.title: I need to modify a platform backend
new_pages.purpose: A recipe for changing a platform backend or the IPlatform contract: ownership of window, event, input and present, the conformance suite, sibling comparison, boundary gates and per-backend test registration.

new_pages.title: I need to add a regression test
new_pages.purpose: A procedure for adding a CNA test: choose the layer, place the file so CMake globs and filters pick it up, write a narrow failing case with negatives, run and confirm registration, plus worked math and content examples.

new_pages.title: I need to modify ContentManager
new_pages.purpose: A recipe for changing ContentManager: the xnb, cnb and loose load ladder, cache key and unload semantics, reader registries, the pipeline-to-runtime contract, error paths, tests and blast radius.

new_pages.title: I need to modify the Content Pipeline
new_pages.purpose: A recipe for changing the content pipeline: importer, processor and writer routes, the cna-content tool and cna_add_content, deterministic output, the XNA facade, the no-device rule, golden round trips and gates.

new_pages.title: I need to update the C API
new_pages.purpose: A maintainer recipe for changing the experimental C ABI: handle and error contracts, version discipline, the checked-in coverage inventory and release gate, pure-C tests, and what a C++ change costs the bindings.

new_pages.title: I need to debug shutdown and lifetime behavior
new_pages.purpose: A maintainer recipe for shutdown and lifetime bugs: which lifetime ended, the destruction order, borrowed pointers, callback barriers, a catalogue of real failure shapes, sanitizers and exit-status harnesses, and a triage.

new_pages.title: I need to investigate a sample failure
new_pages.purpose: A triage flow for a failing XNA sample: the sample ecosystem and its pins, reproducing with the sample's CNA revision, profile, renderer, content, storage and audio axes, and separating a CNA defect from a sample or host fault.

new_pages.title: I need to change build configuration
new_pages.purpose: A maintainer recipe for changing CNA's CMake configuration: option rules, the three selectors and their configure-time refusals and tests, renderer combination rules, presets, CI cells, third-party pins and build-performance policy.

new_pages.title: I need to make a release
new_pages.purpose: A maintainer checklist for cutting a CNA release from the source's own procedure: version sources, generated Version.hpp, changelog and pins, the independent C ABI version and gate, tagging, and what is not established.

new_pages.title: I need to update libcna.com after CNA changes
new_pages.purpose: The maintenance procedure for this site: choose the new CNA commit, compute the delta, map it to pages, recompute the canonical facts, re-read the code, move the pin atomically, regenerate indexes and run every validator.

new_pages.title: Choose one subsystem and own it
new_pages.purpose: A procedure for picking one CNA subsystem and owning it: selection criteria from blast radius, size and tests, verified first candidates, a dossier, a seven-rung ladder and checks that replace reliance on AI.

new_pages.title: Review large AI-generated areas without trusting them
new_pages.purpose: How to read CNA's AI-era paper trail (task IDs, plans, audits, notes, comments) as leads, what its mechanical guards really enforce, and a review method worked on the snapshot's head merge.

new_pages.title: Using the XNA oracle as evidence
new_pages.purpose: What CNA's real-XNA scene corpus is, how a diff is run and judged, what CNA's records claim per renderer and what each gate enforces, when to use it, how to add a scene, and where its evidence stops.

new_pages.title: Source ownership: which part of CNA owns this?
new_pages.purpose: Which CNA module, family or backend owns a behaviour: how the tree encodes ownership, which files are generated, third-party and sibling boundaries, and a 63-row lookup from behaviour to header, source and tests.

new_pages.title: Internals
new_pages.purpose: Source tours of CNA's runtime, graphics, platforms, audio, content, input, modules and C API bindings, pinned to one exact snapshot with ownership, lifetime, failure and test detail.

new_pages.title: OpenGL4 renderer internals
new_pages.purpose: How the OPENGL4 family works: 4.1 core context creation per platform, per-device context isolation, resource lifetime, draw and shader routes, compute and modern additions, capability answers and tests.
